subject.title: Add a slim Docker image mode with configurable APT package installation

question: Should OpenClaw support deployer-configured APT packages for pulled official Docker images, and should that be a derived-image prebuild flow rather than a startup-time installer?
rationale: The implementation choice affects official image hardening, root package-manager execution, package source trust, startup downtime, and the documented env/CLI contract, so code inspection alone cannot choose the boundary.

options.title: Design a derived-image prebuild flow
options.body: Keep this issue open and specify a prebuild command or documented `Dockerfile.extend` pattern that builds from the official image before restarting the gateway.

options.title: Allow a startup-time installer
options.body: Accept the downtime and root package-manager risk by adding an explicit first-boot or entrypoint installer with caching, logging, failure semantics, and clear security docs.

options.title: Keep build-time customization only
options.body: Close or defer this direction and continue steering operators to source/local Docker builds or custom Dockerfiles for extra packages.

recommendation.title: Design a derived-image prebuild flow
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and specify a prebuild command or documented `Dockerfile.extend` pattern that builds from the official image before restarting the gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is a Docker packaging and security-contract decision, and this person has recent adjacent commits hardening and documenting the current APT package build behavior.
